subject: Playbook activation: MAP & POC success plan — CardioSense
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@cardiosense.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T15:15:00Z
Subject: Playbook activation: MAP & POC success plan — CardioSense

Emily — great to meet last week. Per our call, I wanted to start a short MAP thread to align owners, milestones, and success criteria for the upcoming evaluation. I set an initial 6-week POC window below (flexible) and attached a first-pass MAP and a lightweight benchmark sheet for clarity.

High-level goal: validate that Redwood inference can deliver production-grade latency and quality for CardioSense workloads while demonstrating predictable unit cost.

Proposed success criteria (POC):
- Quality: average top-1 prompt pass rate >= 90% on your clinical QA set; core diagnostic prompts >= 95% on sanity checks.
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 250ms for 512-token sequences under typical burst; p99 < 500ms.
- Throughput: sustained 200 RPS within Dedicated/hosted policy or equivalent proxy.
- Cost: unit token cost within target band we discussed (we'll track per-route).

Suggested owners:
- CardioSense (dataset / prompt canonicalization / acceptance): Emily Carter and Anika Shah
- Redwood (benchmark harness / configuration / run leadership): Marcus Lin (SE)
- Redwood (customer success / integration): Monica Patel
- Redwood (commercial / timeline approvals): Laura Bennett
- Executive sponsor: me (Vivek) for any escalation or priority shifts

Tentative timeline:
- Week 0 (Mar 15): kickoff call, access & data-sharing checklist completed
- Week 1: smoke tests + baseline metrics
- Weeks 2–4: sustained bench runs + quality evals (prompt owners provide pass/fail labels)
- Week 5: optimization/quantization runs if needed
- Week 6 (Apr 26): POC review and decision / close or extension

Please confirm the owners above and whether the timeline looks reasonable on your side. If you prefer a hard date window instead of week counts, we can lock Mar 22 — Apr 26.

Attachments: CardioSense_MAP_v1.pdf, redwood_benchmark-sheet.xlsx

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Partnerships & Field GTM
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: CardioSense_MAP_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 2 pages); redwood_benchmark-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 1 sheet)

From: Emily Carter <emily@cardiosense.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@cardiosense.io>, Tom Byrne <tom.byrne@cardiosense.io>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-13T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Playbook activation: MAP & POC success plan — CardioSense

Vivek — thanks for the clear plan and the docs. We’re aligned on the objectives and the owners you listed. A few quick notes from our side:

- I’ll own dataset handoff and prompt canonicalization with Anika. We’ll provide a 2k-record holdout and the 200 canonical prompts you asked for by next Wednesday (Mar 17).
- Anika will lead the quality gating and will prepare the acceptance rubric (pass/fail + confidence band).
- Tom (Ops) will coordinate SSO & network access for the Redwood agents.

One ask: could we push the kickoff by one week to Mar 22 to give the data team extra time to sanitize records? That would move the POC review to the week of Apr 26, which still keeps a 5-week active testing window.

We’ll also upload the initial dataset manifest to the Drive folder you shared and add a short README. I attached our internal compliance checklist for reference.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Emily Carter
Head of Partnerships
CardioSense, Inc.
--
Attachment stubs: CardioSense_Compliance_Checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@cardiosense.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T14:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Playbook activation: MAP & POC success plan — CardioSense

Adding a little operational detail from the SE bench side so everyone knows what to expect. Quoting Emily’s note: "we’ll provide a 2k-record holdout and the 200 canonical prompts" — that’s perfect for our Phase 2 quality harness.

Benchmark phases (high level):
- Phase 0 (pre-kickoff): creds, sample payload shape validation, small smoke (5–10 requests)
- Phase 1 (baseline): single-instance baseline to capture p50/p95/p99 and single-request correctness on canonical prompts
- Phase 2 (scale/throughput): sustained traffic across our Dedicated config to validate sustained p95 goals and observe KV cache behavior
- Phase 3 (quality & regression): run full prompt suite with your labels; compute top-1/top-3 pass rates, hallucination spot checks, and per-prompt failure reasons

Owners (detailed):
- Test harness & runbooks: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.com) — I’ll run the initial baselines and share the run artifacts to the Drive folder.
- Integration & tokens routing: Monica Patel — will coordinate any route-level configs and test keys.
- Commercial check-ins & SLOs: Laura Bennett — will track contract milestones and acceptance.
- Data & labels: Anika Shah (CardioSense) — provides labels and acceptance decisions.

I’ve attached a short runbook and a suggested checklist for Phase 2 runs. Marcus — please confirm if the proposed p95/p99 numbers in Vivek’s note look actionable; we can tighten targets after the smoke.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: benchmark-runbook.md (text/markdown, ~800 bytes)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@cardiosense.io>, Anika Shah <anika.shah@cardiosense.io>, Tom Byrne <tom.byrne@cardiosense.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T18:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Playbook activation: MAP & POC success plan — CardioSense

Appreciate the quick replies and the flexibility on dates. Mar 22 kickoff works for us — I’ll ask Monica to send a calendar invite with a short agenda (access checklist, dataset handoff, owners & immediate actions).

Immediate asks before the kickoff:
- Emily/Anika: upload the dataset manifest + the 200 canonical prompts to the Drive folder and tag which fields are PHI (if any).
- Tom: request SSO test account + IP allowlist for the Redwood test runners (Monica will follow up with a checklist).
- Marcus: prep baseline script and smoke test payloads so we can start immediately on Day 1.

If there are any regulatory constraints that would affect logging or data retention during the POC, flag them in the Drive README so we can scope Private vs Hosted runs.

See you all on the kickoff.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Partnerships & Field GTM
Redwood Inference
